sqlStudy.title: Match selection
sqlStudy.intro: Historical match-selection results with a fixed minimum raw edge of 10 percentage points for both ATP and WTA.
sqlStudy.ruleShort: Include a match only when at least one side has raw edge ≥10 pp, then pick the NN favourite—even if that picked side’s own raw edge is negative.
sqlStudy.payoutShort: Flat 1-unit picks: recorded median odds − 1 on a win; −1 on a loss. Fair odds are a theoretical benchmark, not payout prices.
sqlStudy.riskShort: Historical research, not a guarantee of future profit or proof of executable pre-match prices. Every selected loss and losing period is retained. Source-quote orientation and identity issues remain under review.
sqlStudy.fixedThreshold: Fixed minimum raw edge: ≥10 pp · ATP and WTA
sqlStudy.legacyMin10: Only edge ≥10 pp is displayed. In Summary, edge means NN probability minus the normalized fair-market probability, and the market-undervalued side is selected. This differs from the raw-edge/NN-favourite rule in Match selection. All selected wins, losses and calendar periods are retained.
sqlStudy.demoScope: This demonstration shows selected historical strategies with edge ≥10 pp, not a complete model-performance audit. Positive results in this subset do not establish overall or future profitability.
sqlStudy.quoteQualityWarning: Historical quote review has found unresolved player-identity, price-orientation and source-history issues. Recorded and theoretical fair ROI remain research results, not independently verified achievable returns.
sqlStudy.unavailable: Match-selection results are temporarily unavailable. You can still open the separate Summary view.
sqlStudy.rawRule: For each side, raw edge E = NN probability − 1 / recorded median odds. Keep the match only when max(E1, E2) is at least 0.10 (10 percentage points), including exactly 10 pp. This is a probability-point difference, not a relative percentage; this filter does not remove bookmaker margin.
sqlStudy.favoriteRule: After filtering the match, pick the NN favourite, not the side with the highest edge. The picked side’s own raw edge may be negative. Wins and losses are both retained.
sqlStudy.payoutRule: Recorded-median historical P/L: stake 1 unit per pick; a win returns median odds − 1, a loss −1. This study does not use the Matches Fair/Median toggle. Fair odds are only a theoretical margin-adjusted benchmark, never the payout price here. No Betfair or fair-price payout simulation is included.
sqlStudy.historical: Historical research only: stored odds do not prove an executable pre-match offer, and reconstructed predictions may include in-sample history. These results do not guarantee future profit.
sqlStudy.noOptimization: Fixed historical-research display rule: ATP ≥10 pp / WTA ≥10 pp. Lower thresholds are unavailable. This rule was chosen after reviewing history, not independently validated prospectively.
sqlStudy.sampling: Cumulative end-of-day values; at most 600 displayed points, preserving the first and last. Sampling affects the curve only, not totals, periods or drawdown; intermediate swings may not appear.
sqlStudy.curveDescription: Cumulative historical P/L ending at {{net}} units from {{picks}} picks. Exact period totals are in the following table.
sqlStudy.zeroPicks: No picks at these thresholds. Zero-pick calendar periods remain visible below.
sqlStudy.allPeriods: All supplied years and quarters remain visible, including zero-pick periods and losses. No profitable-period filter is applied.
sqlStudy.candidateCoverageNote: Available candidates count all eligible matches with NN probabilities and paired recorded median odds in that period, before applying the strategy threshold. Zero candidates means eligible NN/odds data are unavailable—not that no tennis was played. — means coverage metadata was not supplied.
sqlStudy.missingCohort: This exact threshold combination is unavailable. No other cohort has been substituted.
sqlStudy.comparisonNote: Both tours use the same fixed raw-edge threshold of ≥10 pp. ALL combines those ATP and WTA selections. No losing match or period is removed from that selection.

competition.rulesBody: Version 1: one final prediction per account and match, up to five new predictions per UTC day. No edits or selective deletion. Each accepted prediction uses one virtual unit at its stored median odds. A correct prediction earns odds minus one; an incorrect prediction loses one unit. The month is fixed by the first submission time (UTC). At least 30 won/lost predictions are required for ranking; voids do not count towards qualification.
competition.resultRules: Submissions close at least five minutes before the trusted scheduled start and whenever status or odds are stale. A later start does not reopen submissions. Cancelled matches, walkovers and retirements are void (0 units). Unverified results remain pending. Delayed results and verified corrections update the original competition month.
competition.fairness: One account per participant. Free entry for verified accounts of every membership tier. Community choices appear only after locking. Model and market comparisons use the information saved at submission; later data updates do not replace it. One successful month is not proof of forecasting skill.
competition.privacy: Your predictions are stored with your account, not sent to Google Analytics. Your nickname and aggregate monthly results are public. Individual picks are private by default. You can share all settled picks in your profile settings, including past wins, losses and voids; open picks remain private. Disabling sharing blocks further access but cannot recall copies already viewed. Account deletion removes your predictions and derived leaderboard results. No real-money rewards are offered.

privacy.title: Your privacy, your choice
privacy.summary: We use browser storage for sign-in, security and your chosen settings. Google Analytics and contributions to BonzoByte's Popularity rankings are separate, optional choices. You can use BonzoByte and view public rankings without allowing either.
privacy.preview: Google Analytics is currently off. Popularity contributions are a separate choice. We will ask again before enabling Google Analytics.
privacy.necessaryText: Session storage supports sign-in, verification and registration through an invitation. The private beta also uses a secure access cookie lasting up to 8 hours. These functions do not depend on either optional consent.
privacy.preferencesText: We remember your chosen theme, language, time zone, filters, table settings and dismissed notices in this browser to provide those functions. Matches you explicitly save as favourites are stored with your account on our server until you remove them or delete your account, so they work across devices. These choices are not sent to Google Analytics. Rejecting optional choices does not reset them.
privacy.analyticsText: When enabled by BonzoByte and accepted here, Google Analytics uses identifiers and cookies to measure visits to the main sections. Google receives technical connection data. We do not send account names, email addresses, payment details or URL tokens in our page-view events. Advertising tracking is not enabled.
privacy.popularityText: With your consent, BonzoByte ranks matches and players using details viewed by signed-in users. Each user contributes at most one view per match or player per UTC day. Short-lived per-user records on our server prevent duplicate counts. Aggregate counts are retained for 28 days; a view's ranking weight halves every 7 days. This feature is processed by our backend and storage providers, not sent to Google Analytics or advertising services. Viewing public rankings never requires consent.
privacy.duration: We remember acceptance and rejection equally for 180 days in this browser, not across devices. Clearing browser storage, expiry or a change in purposes may show this choice again.
privacy.withdraw: You can change either choice here at any time. Withdrawing Google Analytics consent stops future analytics and removes our accessible Analytics cookies. If Analytics was loaded, the page refreshes to stop its running code. Withdrawal does not erase data already received by Google.
privacy.popularityWithdraw: Withdrawing Popularity consent stops new contributions and requests removal of your temporary viewing records. These records also have an automatic expiry 24–48 hours after the view, even if you are offline; database outages or cleanup delays can postpone physical deletion. A temporary record without viewed content prevents further counting until the next UTC midnight, including if you opt back in that day. Existing aggregate counts remain until they expire. Public rankings stay available.
privacy.storageText: Local storage: bonzobyte.privacy.v1 keeps this choice, its date, expiry and policy version; other bonzobyte.* display preferences remain until changed or cleared (a notice snooze may last 30 days). Session storage: token, verifyToken, BB_oauth_token and bonzobyte.referral.pending.v1 support requested account actions; demo-ad dismissals last for the session. Beta cookie: __Host-bonzobyte_beta, up to 8 hours. Optional Analytics cookies: _ga and _ga_Z7VMGXTFFP, limited to the remaining consent period.
privacy.externalText: The page also loads fonts/icons from Google Fonts and Cloudflare CDN; these requests disclose connection data and are separate from Analytics and Popularity. Opening the payment interface loads PayPal, and social sign-in redirects to its provider. These privacy choices control Analytics and Popularity contributions; they do not disable services needed for your account, payments or site operation. Contact us if you have questions about how your data is used.
privacy.referralText: For a registered invited user, BonzoByte checks visits to application sections to validate the trial reward. This first-party membership function is separate from Google Analytics.

body.overviewPurpose: This tab reveals the structured feature groups behind the production model-based match probability shown in the modal. It is designed as a transparency layer, exposing the main input families that contribute to the final prediction instead of presenting the result as a black box.
body.overviewMethod: Rather than relying on a single heuristic or a bookmaker-style shortcut, the displayed probability comes from a curated modelling pipeline built around explicit feature selection, grouped signals, and controlled promotion into the production prediction field.
body.overviewReading: Each sub-section represents one feature family used by the model. Some groups describe the tournament and match context, others reflect core win-probability signals, rating-based strength estimates, normalized transformations, derived precision-style signals, and optional head-to-head inputs.
body.overviewInterpretation: The purpose of this tab is interpretability. It helps advanced users understand that the final probability is generated from a structured analytical system, not from a single opaque score.
body.overviewNotes: The current production setup follows a trusted feature policy, treats ATP and WTA as separate modelling domains, and retains head-to-head information only when it improves the final model profile. The feature groups shown here are a compact view of the promoted model inputs behind the stored match probability.
body.contextMeaning: The Context section captures the match environment around the players rather than the players themselves. It includes tournament structure, playing surface, event strength, round context, and a compact set of competition-level signals that help the model understand where and under what conditions the match takes place.
body.contextPurpose: These inputs provide situational framing for the prediction. They do not attempt to describe player strength directly, but instead supply the surrounding context that can influence how rating-based and probability-based signals should be read.
body.contextReading: Some fields are categorical identifiers such as surface or tournament type, while others are normalized or transformed quantities that represent event strength, surface profile, experience balance, or structural match conditions. Together, they form the environmental layer of the model input.
body.wpMeaning: WP Core contains the central probability-style signals that sit closest to the model’s base match expectation. These values summarize different win-probability perspectives and related rating-informed projections that give the model an immediate sense of which side appears stronger before deeper feature interaction.
body.wpPurpose: This is one of the most direct signal families in the NN view. While it is still only one part of the full model input, it represents the core probabilistic layer on top of which contextual and transformed signals are interpreted.
body.wpReading: Most values in this section are probability-like inputs derived from structured pre-model calculations. They should be understood as calibrated directional signals, not as standalone final predictions. The production probability is generated only after these values are combined with the wider feature set.
body.rawMeaning: Raw TrueSkill contains the direct strength estimates and uncertainty measures used as rating-based inputs for both players. These values describe underlying player quality from the rating system’s perspective before normalization or additional transformations are applied.
body.rawPurpose: In practical terms, this section reflects how the model sees player strength and confidence at the rating layer. It provides one of the main structural foundations for the downstream comparison features used elsewhere in the tab.
body.rawReading: Mean values represent estimated player strength, while SD values represent the remaining uncertainty around that estimate. Because the model consumes multiple rating variants, these inputs are shown as a grouped family rather than as a single score per player.
body.normalizedMeaning: Normalized TrueSkill contains transformed rating-based features that make raw signals easier for the model to compare across matches, players, and competitive contexts. These values help stabilize scale differences and improve consistency when the network processes the broader feature set.
body.normalizedPurpose: This section is less about direct human interpretation and more about preparing rating information in a model-friendly form. It acts as a bridge between raw strength estimates and higher-level derived comparisons.
body.normalizedReading: Values here are typically normalized or transformed versions of rating-based comparisons. They are intended to improve comparability and numerical stability, not to function as standalone headline metrics.
body.derivedMeaning: Derived TrueSkill contains compact comparison features built from the broader rating and probability foundation. These values capture higher-level relationships such as precision-style or weighted comparative signals that can help the model distinguish between superficially similar matches.
body.derivedPurpose: This is a smaller feature family, but it is useful because it compresses more complex rating behaviour into a concise set of structured inputs that the model can consume efficiently.
body.derivedReading: The features shown here are not raw measurements. They are engineered comparison signals derived from upstream rating and probability components, designed to express match-level separation in a more model-friendly way.
body.h2hMeaning: The Head-to-Head section contains historical interaction signals between the two players when that information is included by the promoted model version. These values are treated as a secondary input family rather than as the primary source of the final probability.
body.h2hPurpose: In the current production setup, head-to-head information is retained only where it improves the final model profile. It acts as supporting evidence on top of the broader contextual, probabilistic, and rating-based layers.
body.h2hReading: These inputs summarize prior interaction patterns in a compact way. They can add useful context in some matchups, but they should be read as a complementary signal, not as a substitute for the rest of the model structure.

WP.label: WP
WP.shortDescription: The baseline win probability derived from the global match-level TrueSkill variant, using only the final match winner as the rating outcome signal.

WPS.label: WPS
WPS.shortDescription: The surface-specific version of the baseline win probability, calculated from the same match-level TrueSkill logic but only on the current surface.

WPPondered.label: WP Pondered
WPPondered.shortDescription: A blended win probability currently computed as the simple average of the M, SM, and GSM probability variants rather than as a custom weighted formula.

WPM.label: WPM
WPM.shortDescription: A win probability based on the M rating family, where TrueSkill updates depend only on the final match result and not on sets or games.

WPSM.label: WPSM
WPSM.shortDescription: A win probability based on the SM rating family, where TrueSkill updates take set score into account so a more convincing set margin produces a stronger signal.

WPGSM.label: WPGSM
WPGSM.shortDescription: A win probability based on the GSM rating family, where TrueSkill updates also reflect game-level dominance, making it the most granular of the three core variants.

WPMS.label: WPMS
WPMS.shortDescription: The surface-specific version of WPM, using the match-result-only TrueSkill family restricted to the current surface.

WPSMS.label: WPSMS
WPSMS.shortDescription: The surface-specific version of WPSM, using the set-aware TrueSkill family restricted to the current surface.

WPGSMS.label: WPGSMS
WPGSMS.shortDescription: The surface-specific version of WPGSM, using the game-aware TrueSkill family restricted to the current surface.

P1MeanM.label: P1 Mean M
P1MeanM.shortDescription: Player 1 strength estimate from the M TrueSkill family, where rating updates use only the final match winner.

P1MeanSM.label: P1 Mean SM
P1MeanSM.shortDescription: Player 1 strength estimate from the SM TrueSkill family, where rating updates also reflect how decisive the match was at the set level.

P1MeanGSM.label: P1 Mean GSM
P1MeanGSM.shortDescription: Player 1 strength estimate from the GSM TrueSkill family, where rating updates also reflect game-level dominance and margin.

P1MeanMS.label: P1 Mean MS
P1MeanMS.shortDescription: The surface-specific version of Player 1 M strength, calculated only from matches on the current surface.

P1MeanSMS.label: P1 Mean SMS
P1MeanSMS.shortDescription: The surface-specific version of Player 1 SM strength, calculated only from matches on the current surface.

P1MeanGSMS.label: P1 Mean GSMS
P1MeanGSMS.shortDescription: The surface-specific version of Player 1 GSM strength, calculated only from matches on the current surface.

H2H_WPw_G_TotalPrec.label: H2H Weighted Precision G

This legacy full-history summary is descriptive and must not be interpreted as an untouched out-of-sample test of the current versioned model.
copy.consensusFirstTakesEachBookmakerSMedianA: Consensus first takes each bookmaker's median across its clean snapshots, then the median of those bookmaker medians. Best-price assumes access to the strongest recorded offer and is an intentionally optimistic upper bound.

copy.everyEligibleWagerInTheFullStoredPredict: Every eligible wager in the full stored prediction/odds overlap is included in the calculation. The line retains the exact end-of-day bankroll state in chronological order, avoiding redundant intraday pixels while preserving the full first-to-last date range and ending result. Both player sides are evaluated from complementary model probabilities; only a positive raw-EV side meeting the selected edge threshold enters these curves. Kelly and bounded staking start from a 1,000 bankroll; all three charts show cumulative profit so each begins at zero. Results before the registered out-of-sample boundary are descriptive in-sample/calibration history, not unbiased evidence of future performance. Long-horizon percentage and Kelly compounding are mathematical stress scenarios; their exponential totals are not a realistic capital forecast.
copy.eachRowIsRecomputedFromEveryWagerInThatC: Each row is recomputed from every wager in that calendar segment before browser trajectory compaction. “After registered boundary” means only that the match date follows the stored test/acceptance boundary; it does not turn backfilled predictions or undated odds into prospective evidence.

copy.bonzobyteSNeuralNetworkProbabilitiesOutp: BonzoByte’s neural-network probabilities outperform the market baseline on probabilistic metrics such as Brier score and log loss. The strongest overall performance comes from blending NN and market probabilities rather than relying on either source alone. The optimal blend is not uniform across segments: ATP tends to benefit from a more balanced blend, while WTA consistently performs better with a stronger NN contribution. The largest relative edge appears on weaker WTA tournaments, where NN-heavy blending provides the strongest uplift over market-implied probabilities.

home.aFullStackTennisAnalyticsPlatformBuiltAr: A full-stack tennis analytics platform built around large-scale historical data, advanced rating systems, neural-network probabilities, and a high-performance Brotli archive delivery pipeline.
home.featureRichModelingFoundationWithACurate: Feature-rich modeling foundation with a curated NN subset for production inference.
home.separateStrengthSignalsAcrossResultGranu: Separate strength signals across result granularities and surface-specific contexts.
home.largeHistoricalDatasetsAreDeliveredAsCom: Large historical datasets are delivered as compressed static archives for near-zero runtime chatter.
home.predictionIsEvaluatedSeriouslyThroughPro: Prediction is evaluated seriously through probabilistic metrics, segmentation, and research summaries.
home.bonzobyteIsAResearchDrivenTennisAnalytic: BonzoByte is a research-driven tennis analytics platform that combines a local ASP.NET Core / C# data engine, a normalized relational database, advanced statistical modeling, neural-network inference, and an Angular frontend optimized for fast archive-based exploration.
home.heavyComputationOfflineFastDeliveryOnlin: Heavy computation offline, fast delivery online
home.theCoreOfTheProjectIsALocal: The core of the project is a local ASP.NET Core / C# backend that scrapes, parses, validates, and enriches tennis data before writing it into a structured relational model.
home.dataIngestionAndConsolidationFromMultipl: Data ingestion and consolidation from multiple sources
home.parsingAndValidationOfMatchesPlayersTour: Parsing and validation of matches, players, tournaments, and odds
home.generationOfDerivedStatisticsRatingHisto: Generation of derived statistics, rating histories, and model inputs
home.exportOfOptimizedJSONPayloadsAndCompress: Export of optimized JSON payloads and compressed Brotli archives
home.theBackendUsesANormalizedRelationalDatab: The backend uses a normalized relational database as the clean, maintainable source of truth. This keeps ingestion and feature generation strict, while archive payloads are intentionally denormalized later for fast client consumption.
home.normalizedSchemaForConsistencyAndMaintai: Normalized schema for consistency and maintainability
home.denormalizedArchiveOutputsForFrontendSpe: Denormalized archive outputs for frontend speed
home.clearSeparationBetweenOperationalModelin: Clear separation between operational modeling and presentation data
home.bonzobyteComputesADeeplyGranularTrueSkil: BonzoByte computes a deeply granular TrueSkill layer across match result, set result, and game result dimensions.
home.ratingsAreTrackedNotOnlyGloballyButAlso: Ratings are tracked not only globally, but also by surface, allowing player strength to be represented as context-sensitive rather than flat.
home.historicalMetricsAreAggregatedAcrossOver: Historical metrics are aggregated across overall, weekly, monthly, and yearly scopes, creating a richer player and matchup representation.
home.neuralNetworkProbabilitiesBuiltOnEnginee: Neural-network probabilities built on engineered features
home.theEmphasisIsNotOnlyOnPredictionBut: The emphasis is not only on prediction, but also on disciplined feature selection, signal quality, and evaluation against market baselines.
home.becauseTheOverwhelmingMajorityOfTheDatas: Because the overwhelming majority of the dataset is historical and effectively immutable, BonzoByte delivers most information as static Brotli-compressed archives rather than querying a live database on every interaction.
home.detailedMatchArchivesWithHundredsOfAttri: Detailed match archives with hundreds of attributes
home.indexArchivesForFastSearchAndFiltering: Index archives for fast search and filtering
home.trueskillHistoryArchivesForChartRenderin: TrueSkill history archives for chart rendering
home.rawJSONPayloadsCanBeDramaticallyLargerTh: Raw JSON payloads can be dramatically larger than their Brotli-packed equivalents. That reduces transfer cost, avoids unnecessary roundtrips, and allows many interactions to happen entirely in client memory.
home.nearZeroRuntimeDependencyOnTheHistorical: Near-zero runtime dependency on the historical data store
home.customBrotliViewerDecompressionLayerInsi: Custom Brotli viewer / decompression layer inside the frontend
home.angularAsASeriousClientApplication: Angular as a serious client application
home.theAngularFrontendFetchesDecompressesAnd: The Angular frontend fetches, decompresses, and presents archive content on demand, turning mostly static datasets into a responsive product experience.
home.matchesPlayersTournamentsAnalyticsDashbo: Matches, players, tournaments, analytics dashboards, and model insight pages are presented through route-level pages, shared modal architecture, and rich detail views.
home.indexArchivesCanBeLoadedOnceAndThen: Index archives can be loaded once and then searched or filtered instantly on the client, with no repeated backend roundtrips.
home.predictionIsOnlyPartOfTheStory: Prediction is only part of the story
home.mongodbIsUsedForAccountConcernsSuchAs: MongoDB is used for account concerns such as registration, login, verification, password reset, user state, and application-level identity workflows.
home.thePlatformSupportsClassicCredentialBase: The platform supports classic credential-based authentication as well as OAuth providers, using JWT-based session handling in the application layer.
home.separationBetweenHeavyOfflineComputation: Separation between heavy offline computation and lightweight online delivery
home.strictDependencyInjectionAndServiceBound: Strict dependency injection and service boundaries
home.normalizedSourceDataWithIntentionalDenor: Normalized source data with intentional denormalized read models
home.archiveFirstStrategyForMostlyImmutableDa: Archive-first strategy for mostly immutable datasets
home.reusableUIPatternsAndSharedModalArchitec: Reusable UI patterns and shared modal architecture
home.strongFocusOnMaintainabilityExplainabili: Strong focus on maintainability, explainability, and scalability
home.futureModelIterationsWillIncorporateAddi: Future model iterations will incorporate additional statistical inputs such as aces, double faults, return winners, and other deeper performance signals.
home.existingMarkovChainWorkCanBeConnectedTo: Existing Markov-chain work can be connected to live match states to estimate win probability and final score paths before and during matches.
home.plannedWorkIncludesStrongerFallbackCover: Planned work includes stronger fallback coverage, doubles support, more advanced explainability, and deeper model interpretation layers such as SHAP-style analysis.
home.neuralDescription: The platform includes a trained neural-network model built on a curated subset of approximately 75 selected features, chosen from a wider pool of more than 250 engineered candidate variables.
home.researchMetrics: BonzoByte compares neural probabilities against market-implied probabilities and evaluates them using probabilistic metrics such as Brier score and log loss.
home.researchSegments: It also studies blended strategies and segment-specific behavior across tours, surfaces, tournament strength, and favorite / underdog structures — all surfaced through Analytics and Model Insights.
